system.name: PICACHU
system.one_liner: a plug-in coarse-grained reconfigurable accelerator (CGRA) that offloads nonlinear operations in LLM inference

components.name: Systolic Array
components.role: produces matrix-multiplication outputs that feed the Shared Buffer

components.name: Shared Buffer
components.role: SRAM multiplexed from the systolic array's output memory; holds CGRA input/output/statistics/other segments

components.name: SPM Crossbar
components.role: crossbar switch routing data between Shared Buffer segments and the CGRA

components.name: PICACHU CGRA
components.role: executes the nonlinear operation, reading from and writing to the Shared Buffer

components.name: DRAM
components.role: off-chip memory read via DMA when the Shared Buffer cannot hold an entire tensor

components.name: CGRA Input
components.role: Shared Buffer segment holding data to be consumed by the CGRA

components.name: CGRA Output
components.role: Shared Buffer segment holding results produced by the CGRA

components.name: Statistics
components.role: Shared Buffer segment holding intermediate reduction statistics such as mean and variance

components.name: Other
components.role: Shared Buffer segment holding other variables

flows.what: output streamed via the on-chip crossbar each round, Case 1 (element-wise ops)
element-wise results written back without buffering intermediates, Case 1
inputs retrieved channel-by-channel via DMA when the buffer cannot hold the tensor, Case 2 (reduction ops)
intermediate statistics such as mean and variance buffered across rounds, Case 2

content.key_idea: The Shared Buffer, multiplexed from the systolic array's output SRAM, either streams data straight to the CGRA through an on-chip crossbar (element-wise ops) or pulls it via DMA from DRAM while buffering statistics (reduction ops).
content.reading_order: Left to right from the systolic-array/Shared-Buffer schematic into a grid of Round 1-3 columns by Case 1-2 rows, read top-to-bottom then left-to-right, with a legend below.

palette.used_for: neutral background fill of the SA boxes and systolic-array schematic
one of the Block-labeled arrows tracking data across rounds

style.stroke: medium borders, dashed separating the Round columns and Case rows
style.arrows: many thin colored arrows (xbar/DMA) linking SA to buffer segments, plus three colored Block-labeled arrows tracking data across rounds

encoding.color_means: pink/red = CGRA Input segment, pale yellow = CGRA Output segment, green = Statistics segment, blue = Other segment; orange/teal/gray Block-1/2/3 arrows trace one data item across the three rounds
encoding.line_style_means: xbar (crossbar) vs. DMA labeled arrows distinguish on-chip Shared-Buffer routing (Case 1) from off-chip DRAM transfers (Case 2); 'enable'/'disable' labels mark whether DMA is active that round
encoding.emphasis: the Round1-3 x Case1-2 grid contrasts element-wise operations, which stream straight through the crossbar, against reduction operations, which require DMA and buffered statistics
reusable_patterns: round-by-round timeline grid contrasting two execution cases
colored Shared-Buffer segments (input/output/statistics/other) reused across both cases
weaknesses: a six-cell grid plus a separate schematic and legend is a lot to parse in one figure
Block-1/2/3 arrow colors are explained only in a legend placed below the grid

evidence: We integrate the CGRA with the systolic array by multiplexing the output SRAM of the systolic array.
Each time the systolic array produces output, execution in the CGRA can commence immediately
the inputs for the Shared Buffer are retrieved from off-chip DRAM

summary: This figure shows how the PICACHU CGRA is integrated with the systolic array through a shared, multiplexed SRAM (the Shared Buffer), routed by an SPM crossbar. The buffer is partitioned into CGRA Input, CGRA Output, Statistics and Other segments. A round-by-round grid contrasts two data-flow cases across three rounds: in Case 1 (element-wise operations), the systolic array's output streams straight into the CGRA through the on-chip crossbar each round, with DMA disabled and no intermediate statistics buffered. In Case 2 (reduction operations whose tensor exceeds the buffer), inputs are instead retrieved channel-by-channel from off-chip DRAM via DMA, and intermediate statistics such as mean and variance are kept in the Statistics segment across rounds until the reduction completes. Colored Block-1/2/3 arrows trace one data item's movement through the grid, with a legend explaining the buffer-segment and arrow colors.
summary_zh: 该图展示 PICACHU CGRA 与脉动阵列的集成：共享缓冲含输入/输出/统计/其他四段，经交叉开关连接；Case 1 逐元素算子经片上直通、禁用 DMA，Case 2 归约算子需 DMA 分通道读取 DRAM 并缓存中间统计量。
